claims.text: A predictor is counterfactually fair if its distribution over possible predictions for an individual remains unchanged under a counterfactual intervention on protected attributes.
A predictor is counterfactually fair if it is constructed as a function of non-descendants of the protected attributes in the causal graph.
Omitting protected attributes while regressing on observable features (fairness through unawareness) fails to achieve counterfactual fairness in Scenario 1.
In a linear model under Scenario 1, regressing the outcome on both protected attributes and observable features produces a counterfactually fair predictor.
The Full model using all features achieved an RMSE of 0.873 on the law school success dataset.
The Unaware model achieved an RMSE of 0.894 on the law school success dataset.
The Level 2 counterfactually fair model (FairK) achieved an RMSE of 0.929 on the law school success dataset.
The Level 3 counterfactually fair model (Fair Add) achieved an RMSE of 0.918 on the law school success dataset.
Full and Unaware baseline predictors exhibit counterfactual unfairness when evaluating counterfactual race modifications on the law school dataset.

evidence.description: Definition 5 states that P(Y_hat_{A<-a}(U) = y | X=x, A=a) = P(Y_hat_{A<-a'}(U) = y | X=x, A=a) for all y and any value a' attainable by A.
Lemma 1 proves that any function of non-descendants of A in causal graph G is invariant with respect to counterfactual values of A.
Lemma 3 shows that least-squares regression of Y on X alone yields Y_hat_a(U) = lambda*(alpha*a + beta*U), which depends on a and is not counterfactually fair.
Lemma 3 demonstrates that regressing Y on both X and A yields Y_hat(X, a) = gamma*U, which cancels out changes in X caused by A.

methodologies.name: FAIR LEARNING Algorithm
methodologies.description: An MCMC-based algorithm that samples latent background variables U given observed attributes and optimizes model parameters restricted to non-descendants of protected attributes.
datasets: LSAC National Longitudinal Bar Passage Study dataset
conditions: Stan probabilistic programming for Level 2 posterior inference of latent knowledge
Additive error model for Level 3 residual estimation

limitations.text: Counterfactual assumptions such as structural equations are in general unfalsifiable even when interventional data for all variables is available.
Ensuring counterfactual fairness requires sacrificing a small amount of prediction accuracy compared to models that utilize unfair features.

Existing observational definitions of fairness (such as Demographic Parity and Equality of Opportunity) can be mutually incompatible and may inadvertently increase discrimination depending on protected attribute relationships.
Fairness through unawareness fails because unobserved or remaining observable attributes can carry discriminatory information correlated with protected attributes.

future_work.text: Investigating sensitivity analysis and robustness extensions focusing on approximate versions of counterfactual fairness.
Developing quantitative causal models to evaluate the long-run macroeconomic impacts and feedback mechanisms of localized fair decision-making on societal biases.
